experiments.question: Can a bundled AI-native-vs-legacy comparison falsely attribute gains to model-native symbolic language when the actual gains come from intent compilation, canonical IR and deterministic runtime?
experiments.construction: Balanced 2^4 factorial. Base success 0.42; planted I +0.06, C +0.16, R +0.11, CxR +0.03. Two scenarios: N-null with native main/interactions exactly zero; N-present with native main +0.07 and CxN +0.04. 30 local seeds x 10,000 observations/cell.
experiments.interpretation: In the constructed native-null world, a bundled AI-native comparison reports a large ~0.36 gain despite exactly zero planted native-symbol effect; orthogonal intervention correctly recovers approximately zero. When a native effect is planted, orthogonal analysis recovers it and the CxN interaction. Therefore AI-native language must be factorized by layer before causal attribution.
experiments.boundary: Synthetic calibration only; magnitudes are planted/workload-specific and are not FRANK/Qwen estimates.

experiments.question: Can a highly semantically pure discrete symbol codebook be causally irrelevant to model output?
experiments.construction: Four balanced classes. A synthetic discrete symbol matches the class about 95% of the time, producing high modal-label symbol purity. Output is generated independently by a separate latent predictor at about 80% accuracy; the symbol is unused by construction. 30 seeds x 50,000 observations.
experiments.interpretation: High purity/semantic alignment can arise for a monitored or explicitly supervised codebook without the symbol carrying causal control of the decision. Purity, convergence and human-readable symbol chains therefore require lesion/permutation/rescue/OOD tests before being called a reasoning mechanism.
experiments.boundary: Constructed null, not a claim about the AIM papers' implementation. It demonstrates a confound their metrics must rule out.
